title: 'The Vvaan' Adds Rs 2.50 Crore in Third Weekend as Theatrical Run Nears Its End
excerpt: The Sidharth Malhotra folk-fantasy is closing on 'Student of the Year' to become his fourth-highest grosser, though trackers disagree on whether its India net stands at Rs 62 crore or Rs 67 crore.
body:
• "The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest" collected Rs 2.50 crore in India in its third weekend, according to Pinkvilla, as its theatrical run winds down.
  • Tracker totals differ by methodology: Sacnilk puts the film at Rs 67.35 crore India net and Rs 87.66 crore worldwide gross, while Pinkvilla's running total is lower, near Rs 62 crore net.
  • The folk-fantasy thriller has passed Sidharth Malhotra's "Param Sundari" and is closing on "Student of the Year" (Rs 70 crore) to become his fourth-highest grosser.
  • Bihar emerged as a standout market, powered by the film's Chhath Puja sequence and the song "Chhathi Maiya."

"The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest" is finishing its theatrical run the way it ran throughout: steadily, respectably, and ahead of the low expectations it opened with. The Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia starrer collected Rs 2.50 crore in India across its third weekend, according to Pinkvilla, bringing a three-week run that began on September 25 toward its close.

The numbers, with their disagreements attached

Box-office totals for the film vary by tracker, and the differences are worth stating rather than smoothing over. Sacnilk, the industry tracker, credits the film with Rs 67.35 crore net in India and Rs 87.66 crore gross worldwide — the basis for The Week's report that it is nearing Rs 90 crore worldwide. Pinkvilla's day-by-day ledger runs lower, at roughly Rs 62 crore net after the third weekend. Trade estimates compiled elsewhere put the India net between Rs 64 crore and Rs 65 crore, against a reported production budget of about Rs 80 crore — which leaves the film's final verdict dependent on which ledger, and which revenue streams beyond theatres, are counted.

"The folk-fantasy thriller has passed Sidharth Malhotra's "Param Sundari" and is closing on "Student of the Year" (Rs 70 crore) to become his fourth-highest grosser."

Malhotra's best in years

On any of those ledgers, the film is a personal milestone. Variety India notes it has passed "Student of the Year" (Rs 70 crore lifetime, within reach this week) territory to become Malhotra's fourth-highest grosser, behind "Ek Villain" (Rs 105.76 crore), "Brothers" (Rs 82.49 crore) and "Kapoor & Sons" (Rs 73.22 crore) — and it delivered his biggest opening weekend in 11 years, Rs 33.25 crore net in three days. It opened better than his post-pandemic releases "Thank God" and "Yodha," from a base of modest advance bookings.

Why it worked where it worked

The film, directed by Deepak Kumar Mishra — a co-director of "Panchayat" — follows Rishi, an engineer who returns to his ancestral village in Bihar and is drawn into the legend of a goddess who guards a forbidden forest. Its rootedness became its marketing. Bihar contributed a significant share of collections, helped by the depiction of Chhath Puja and the song "Chhathi Maiya," which connected with audiences in the state where the festival is a defining event. With no major new Hindi release this Friday, the film retains a workable number of screens for its final stretch. For diaspora viewers who missed it in theatres, an OTT announcement has not yet been made — the theatrical window is the only confirmed way to see it for now.
